key_insight: Orbitol generates crystals using Wyckoff-orbit tokens, explicitly controlling space-group symmetry while sampling chemistry, coordinates and lattice geometry.
engineering_relevance: Symmetry-controlled generation can target crystal classes that permit useful responses such as piezoelectricity, narrowing materials screening toward functional candidates.
method: Replace atom tokens in the Crystalite diffusion Transformer with Wyckoff-orbit tokens.
Condition on a space group and occupied Wyckoff positions to generate atom types, free coordinates and a compatible lattice.
Evaluate symmetry retention and distribution agreement with the proposed SPARC score.
evidence_signal: On MP-20, 13.8% of attempts produced stable or metastable, unique, novel crystals retaining the requested symmetry after relaxation, versus 10.8% for SGFM; generation was 100–1,000× faster than symmetry-aware baselines at evaluated settings.
watch_item: Symmetry by construction does not guarantee retention after relaxation or physical viability; the reported 89% DFT pass rate applies only to internally screened piezoelectric candidates.
paper_title: Orbitol: Crystal Generation on Wyckoff Orbits
